notes: VP Eng: 'We need near-real-time responses for agent flows; users hate >300ms lag on first tokens.'
Primary workload: multi-step agentic workflows — search -> summarize -> take action (open ticket, tag, escalate).
Key metric: end-to-end p95 initial-token latency <= 250ms for streaming in EU/US regions; throughput bursts up to 200 rps in peaks.
Tool-calling concerns: timeouts and partial failures leave agent in inconsistent state — want guaranteed at-most-once or clear compensating actions.
Preference: start on Hosted API for fast POC (timeboxing), then evaluate Dedicated for predictable throughput and reserved slots.
Cost sensitivity: estimates for 5M tokens/month + 150 concurrent sessions during business hours — looking for committed pricing and burst options.
Observability: needs token-level traces, function-call logs, per-route latency breakdowns. Want Redwood Console access for POC.
Asked for example configs: continuous batching settings, KV cache TTL recommendations, fallback routing policy samples.
Legal/security: requires DPA updates, data residency for EU customers, optional on-prem for regulated accounts down the road.
use_case_summary: Mid-market SaaS product team building an ops agent for customer support teams. The agent performs a multi-step flow: ingest support context, search internal KB + logs, summarize findings, and open/escalate tickets via internal APIs. Needs streaming responses and function/tool calling. Primary concerns: streaming latency (p95 initial token <=250ms), tool-call reliability (timeouts/retries/idempotency), and cost predictability. Starting with Hosted API POC; target Dedicated if throughput and deterministic latency are required.
